subject: Sealed-network operator access and egress controls — Corundum RFI clarifications
messages:
From: Corundum Health Procurement <procurement@corundumhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Sep 2028 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Corundum RFI: sealed-network operator access and egress controls

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking our RFI. We've reviewed the materials so far and have three technical clarifications we need before routing to our security committee:

1) Operator access model: can Redwood operators access isolated/private deployments for troubleshooting? If so, what access modality do you use (bastion, break-glass, vendor-controlled jump host), are sessions time-limited, and is MFA enforced?

2) Egress controls: can the runtime open outbound connections from the sealed environment for telemetry or package updates? If yes, what destinations and protocols are allowed, and how are those connections authorized and audited?

3) Audit and evidence: what logs are generated for operator sessions and egress events, what retention periods do you support, and can logs be exported to a customer-managed SIEM?

Attached: Corundum_RFI_v3.xlsx (worksheet: Section C - Sealed Network).

We'd like consolidated answers by COB Monday 9/4 if possible — the security committee meeting is Tue 9/5.

Regards,
Corundum Procurement Team
--
Corundum Health
procurement@corundumhealth.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Corundum RFI: sealed-network operator access and egress controls

Hi team,

Thanks for the clear questions — appreciate the deadline. High-level answers below; attached is a 2-page summary (sealed_network_summary.pdf) and I've looped in Ben and Grace for technical depth. We'll produce a consolidated pack tomorrow.

1) Operator access model:
- Redwood supports customer-managed sealed deployments with zero standing operator access.
- When operator assistance is required (break-glass), access is provided via a customer-hosted bastion or an in-customer jump host that you control; Redwood does not maintain persistent inbound connectivity.
- Access requests are time-limited (typically 1-hour windows) and require explicit customer approval; all sessions require MFA and are brokered through an auditable access workflow.

2) Egress controls:
- By default our sealed runtime does not initiate outbound connections except to customer-approved endpoints.
- Optional egress flows (package updates, telemetry) can be configured via allowlist to specific IPs/FQDNs and ports. Updates are delivered via signed artifacts only and can be staged through a customer-controlled update relay.

3) Audit and evidence:
- Operator session recording (command logs + session metadata), egress connection logs (source/target, protocol, bytes), and runtime telemetry are retained per contract; standard retention is 90 days and can be extended.
- Logs can be shipped to a customer-managed SIEM over TLS to a provided endpoint; we also provide a downloadable evidence bundle for audits.

Attachment: sealed_network_summary.pdf

Ben/Grace — can you add the network diagram and confirm retention SLAs?

Best,
Naomi

Subject: Re: Corundum RFI: sealed-network operator access and egress controls

Naomi — copying the relevant technical details below (quoting your note for context):

> "When operator assistance is required (break-glass), access is provided via a customer-hosted bastion or an in-customer jump host that you control; Redwood does not maintain persistent inbound connectivity."

Confirmed. A few implementation specifics for Corundum's security committee:
- Access flow: Customer opens ticket -> approves access window in console -> temporary credential issued (PKI-backed short-lived cert) -> operator connects to customer bastion. No direct Redwood inbound IPs are permitted by default.
- Protocols: SSH (with port-forwarding disabled unless pre-approved), HTTPS (for agent pull), and an SFTP overlay for file exchange when needed. All operator traffic traverses the customer bastion and is restricted by network ACLs.
- Session controls: Sessions are MFA + certificate-based, logged at both the bastion and the runtime. We support live session recording (optional), and command-level logs are hashed and fingerprinted for tamper evidence.
- KMS integration: Customer keys remain in your KMS (we support AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, and HSM exports); operator-invoked decryption requires an ephemeral KMS grant only valid during the approved window.
- Egress gating: Runtime components have egress routes collapsed to an allowlist. For package updates we recommend a customer-side update relay (pull model) that validates signed artifacts; telemetry is buffered locally and exported to an allowlisted endpoint.

Attachment: network_diagram_v2.svg (shows bastion -> runtime -> update-relay pattern).

Retention notes (from infra): default 90 days for telemetry and session metadata; audit bundles can be exported as a signed tarball for longer-term archival. If Corundum requires 365-day retention we can add a commercial option in the SOW.

Irene — confirm the SIEM export endpoints we support and the expected TLS cipher suites.

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Corundum RFI: sealed-network operator access and egress controls — consolidated answers

Hi Corundum team,

Appended below is a consolidated response to the three items you flagged. We also uploaded a full response pack and diagrams to the shared Drive and included a downloadable evidence bundle.

Short answers:
1) Operator access: No standing access. Break-glass only via customer bastion; time-limited, MFA and PKI-backed certs; full session logging and optional recording.
2) Egress controls: Default-deny; allowlist model for updates/telemetry; signed artifacts and customer-side update relay recommended.
3) Audit & evidence: Command-level logs, session metadata, egress logs; standard 90-day retention; exportable to customer SIEM; audit bundles downloadable.

Longer form and attachments: we uploaded the full RFI response pack (rfi_response_pack.zip) and the updated network diagram to the folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_Redwood-Corundum-RFI

If you need a redline to the SOW for the extended retention option or a sample KMS grant workflow, we can prepare those before your security meeting. For documentation flow we've also sent a DocuSign link for the mutual NDA amendment you requested: https://www.docusign.com/RC/1234-Abc-Redwood-RFI

Attachment: rfi_response_pack.zip

Quoted for context:
> "Access requests are time-limited (typically 1-hour windows) and require explicit customer approval; all sessions require MFA and are brokered through an auditable access workflow."

If you can confirm the emergency workflow (and any limitations on scope during emergency windows) that will help our process notes.
